overclaims: Accuracy was a real commercialization barrier: BCG found it the leading reported obstacle in information services.
But adoption and reported benefits were increasing.
checks.note: The rationale calls accuracy a 'real' barrier, but BCG only reports the most-cited perceived barrier; the payload's own limitation says surveys don't isolate causes. Deloitte reports more investment because of value, not that benefits were increasing. The e2 excerpt and locator (Exhibit 4) cover respondents' personal use, but the explanation cites 65% organisational use, which neither shows. Axis, horizon and outcome (unresolved) match the reviews.

overclaims: SimpleQA selects difficult questions and tests short answers without browsing.
The evaluation was conducted by a model developer and uses automated grading with human checks.
checks.note: The rationale and the e1 citation are supported, and the outcome (supported, historical_observation) matches the reviews. But two limitations go beyond the evidence. 'Without browsing' appears nowhere in it. 'Human checks' of grading isn't shown either: two AI trainers set the reference answers, and the paper describes model-based grading only. Remove these or support them with evidence.
